name: install
description: The file(s) are copied to the target file or directory. If the destination is a directory, then the file is copied into directory with its original filename.

options.name: -B
options.description: Use suffix as the backup suffix if -b is given

options.name: -b
options.description: Back up any existing files before overwriting them by renaming them to file.old. See -B for specifying a different backup suffix

options.name: -C
options.description: Copy the file.  If the target file already exists and the files are the same, then don't change the modification time of the target

options.name: -c
options.description: Copy the file.  This is actually the default.  The -c option is only included for backwards compatibility

options.name: -d
options.description: Create directories.  Missing parent directories are created as required

options.name: -f
options.description: Specify the target's file flags; see chflags(1) for a list of possible flags and their meanings

options.name: -g
options.description: Specify a group. A numeric GID is allowed

options.name: -m
options.description: Specify an alternate mode.  The default mode is set to rwxr-xr-x (0755).

options.name: -o
options.description: Specify an owner. A numeric UID is allowed

options.name: -p
options.description: Preserve the modification time. Copy the file, as if the -C (compare and copy) option is specified, except if the target file doesn't already exist or is differ…

options.name: -S
options.description: Safe copy. Normally, install unlinks an existing target before installing the new file.

options.name: -s
options.description: Exec's the command strip(1) to strip binaries so that install can be portable over a large number of systems and binary types

options.name: -v
options.description: Causes install to show when -C actually installs something

args.name: file1 file2 | file1 ... fileN directory | directory ...
